title: A field's own bit order is the effective one, and a change of order starts a new byte
description: The struct is LSBFirst; a declares MSBFirst and is written in the top three bits of the first byte (101 00000 = A0, the unused bits 0). b, back under LSBFirst, differs in order from a, so it begins on the next byte, in its low five bits: 16. (The parse case pp-bits-field-order-overrides-struct reads B4 16 as this tree; the bits it skips are written as 0.)
